target_moa.text: Mirdametinib is a small molecule inhibitor of MEK1 and MEK2 (mitogen-activated protein kinases 1 and 2), upstream regulators of the ERK pathway; it inhibited MEK1 and MEK2 kinase activity with Ki values of 1.1 nM and 0.79 nM, respectively, and reduced neurofibroma growth in an NF1 mouse model

citations.quote: Mirdametinib is a small molecule inhibitor of mitogen-activated protein kinases 1 and 2 (MEK1/2). MEK1/2 proteins are upstream regulators of the extracellular signal-related kinase (ERK) pathway.
In biochemical assays, mirdametinib inhibited the kinase activity of MEK1 and MEK2 with inhibitory constant (Ki) values of 1.1 nM and 0.79 nM, respectively.
In a mouse model of NF1, oral dosing of mirdametinib inhibited ERK phosphorylation and reduced neurofibroma tumor volume and proliferation.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>25%) were rash, diarrhea, nausea, musculoskeletal pain, vomiting, and fatigue; most common Grade 3/4 laboratory abnormality (>2%) was increased creatine phosphokinase. In the pooled safety population rash occurred in 84% (31% Grade 2, 6% Grade 3). Permanent discontinuation due to an adverse reaction occurred in 22% of adult patients.

citations.quote: The most common adverse reactions (>25\%) were rash, diarrhea, nausea, musculoskeletal pain, vomiting, and fatigue. The most common Grade 3 or 4 laboratory abnormality (>2\%) was increased creatine phosphokinase.
In the pooled safety population [see *Adverse Reactions (6.1)*], rash occurred in 84% of patients treated with GOMEKLI: 31% were Grade 2, and 6% were Grade 3.
Permanent discontinuation of GOMEKLI due to an adverse reaction occurred in 22% of adult patients.

summary.text: Mirdametinib received regular (traditional) approval for NF1-associated symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas based on overall response rate and duration of response from the single-arm ReNeu study. The application was a priority review NDA and had Orphan Drug (30Oct2018), Fast Track (28May2019), and Rare Pediatric Disease (24Jul2023) designations.

citations.quote: The review team recommends regular approval of mirdametinib for the treatment of adult and pediatric patients 2 years of age and older with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) who have symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas not amenable to complete surgical resection.

FDA considers ORR, supported by DOR, to be an appropriate endpoint for regular approval for this rare patient population given that their clinical meaningfulness is associated with improved clinical outcome assessment data from the ReNeu study.
